item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-29
item.description: At the OpenHarmony Technical Conference in Nanjing on 2026-11-28, the chair of OpenAtom's board said the state had approved renaming the foundation 'OpenAtom International Open Source Foundation' (开放原子国际开源基金会), with internationalisation written into its core mission — while the same speech committed it to spending no less than CNY 150 million a year on a single project, OpenHarmony. This briefing reads the rename against the things a foundation actually needs in order to be international: legal personality abroad, a published charter, a membership with votes, and work a foreign maintainer can do. Four sub-national instruments landed beside it on the same day — a nine-task municipal action plan with a CNY 100 billion revenue target, a municipal reception centre, a ceremony awarding compatibility-assessment partner status, and a corporate programme that pays partners to adopt. Chinese open source now has an active, funded, locally governed federation with no accessible membership route, and the org chart, read carefully, is the governance.
